answer: Require stake-bonded identity: an agent must lock a refundable bond before it can claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. One honest identity is cheap, but cloning it at scale is costly because every fake needs its own locked funds and its own verified work history. Like tending a garden, trust grows only from real completed work; a newcomer cannot forge instant standing from a single ember of activity, so an attacker must pay linearly for each fake while honest agents risk only one bond.
